title: COMING Saturday May 9th | You Can Call Me Paul (A Paul Simon Tribute)
location: Pisgah Brewing Company Black Mountain, 2948 US-70, Black Mountain, NC, 28711
description:
You Can Call Me Paul | May 9, 2026 7:00 PM | $31+ Event Details and Tickets
Benjamin Falcon formed a love of the Simon & Garfunkel songbook while growing up outside of DC, in Alexandria, VA, through his parents fondness and nostalgia for Simon’s early work, as well as Falcon’s frequent exposure to the music in radio and media. In college, Falcon began to explore the larger catalogue of both Simon’s early and solo material.
“You can call me Paul” has since sold out venues and attracted the collaboration of nationally touring musicians of note, including Jason Hann (The String Cheese Incident), Justin Ray (Michael Bublé), Justin Stanton (Snarky Puppy).
This twelve-member band was assembled to authentically recreate the experience of seeing Simon’s solo work through the eras, in a live setting, with all the power and emotion that drew you to start.
  
Founded in 2005, Pisgah is known for producing some of the most sought after craft ales in Western North Carolina. Pisgah Brewing Company currently operates the new indoor taproom & deli, with live music several days a week, plus an open air outdoor bar in the summer and fall months. title: Spring Mind-Body Wellness Retreat
description:
Spring Mind-Body Wellness Retreat
with Jenne Sluder 
Tuesday, April 28  |  10 am – 4pm 
REGISTER HERE 
Set aside a day for quiet reflection and renewal at the North Carolina Arboretum, centering themes from the poetry of Mary Oliver. Calm your mind, refresh your spirit, and relax your body and nervous system with a gentle immersion into mind-body centering practices both indoors and in nature. Expect slow, mindful yoga and qigong, guided meditation, progressive relaxation + sound bath, contemplative readings from Mary Oliver, and time for personal journaling and quiet time in nature. All mind-body practices will be gentle and accessible, including the choice to do any seated movements or meditations in a chair or on a cushion according to your own body’s needs. 
Jenne Sluder, MA C-IAYT holds a Master’s in Transpersonal Psychology: Ecopsychology from Naropa University. She is a certified yoga therapist, mind-body specialist, and meditation instructor. Jenne is also an environmental educator and spent her undergrad years working and studying under the direct mentorship of Thomas Berry and Joseph Cornell at the Center for Education, Imagination, and the Natural World, continuing her studies in nature-based rites of passage with the School of Lost Borders and the Earth-Based Institute. An Asheville native, Jenne works one-on-one with individuals and with groups using mindfulness-based, nature-based, and compassion-centric mind-body therapies towards personal and collective well-being.

title: Spirited Improv Community Playshop
description:
Awakening Asheville
### SPIRITED IMPROV Community Playshop:

This is not traditional improvisation. Imagine Spirited Improv as a spiritual practice, where creativity meets consciousness and community. No experience necessary.

**ABOUT SPIRITED IMPROV**

Spirited Improv is a unique fusion of expressive arts, spiritual practice, and group play that helps you release fear, trust the unknown, and show up as your truest self.
Spirited Improv is a soul-centered community experience that uses improvisational play as the container for spiritual growth, personal transformation, and authentic connection. Rather than focusing on comedy or performance, we use improv as a living practice, one that invites presence, trust, curiosity, and responsiveness in the moment.

Facilitated by Jessica Chilton, who brings over 20 years of improvisational performing arts experience and 16 years as an expressive arts therapist, weaving creativity, spirituality, and presence into a safe, transformative group experience.

**2 HR COMMUNITY PLAYSHOP**
This special session takes place on the final day of the current Spirited Improv series, when we open the experience to the wider community.
You’ll join the participants who have been playing together throughout the series. You’re welcome to watch from the audience and enjoy the unfolding experience, or jump in and participate in the improvisational play alongside the group.

This is a beautiful way to experience Spirited Improv before joining a future series.

**WHAT PAST PARTICIPANTS ARE SAYING**

“Spirited Improv is authentic, vulnerable and connective. It meets my need to deeply feel, be seen and see others. On my first night I experienced such a profound healing experience after sharing what was on my heart. It was like a sound, healing touch, full moon energy bath that opened my heart. ” \~ Kate

“Spirited Improv is a fun and little bit edgy way of interacting with the mystery of the moment. You decide how much you want to interact or observe from the audience so you never have to do anything you don't want to do. It is an opportunity to let go of control and explore the spontaneity of life and creativity in a supportive, safe environment..” \~ Kenyon

“I got to play, move my body, laugh, take joy in watching my friends come alive, give and receive big hugs, and feel the presence of the ancestors who always join me. There’s something so sacred about being present with others while we play, witness and embody what is.” \~ Sue

$$$PAY WHAT YOU WANT OPTION $$$

More info at https://spiritedimprov.com

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: Ukrainian Pysanky Easter egg workshop
location: Studio A
description:
Pysanky are a lot like Asheville- unique, fun and colorful!



In this workshop we will be making beautiful Ukrainian Easter eggs – pysanky. You will learn the method of batik – also called wax-resist – dying. You will also be familiarized with the wide range of Ukrainian folk art traditional patterns, designs and symbols and their history. The designs are made with beeswax which is melted in the flame of a candle and applied to the egg using a tool called a kistka. The eggs are dipped into successively darker dyes. At the end of the process the beeswax is melted off to reveal the beautiful and colorful design. You may use the traditional patterns, or also freestyle and make up your own design. Pysanky are fun, relaxing, and meditative to create. And, the symbols are all good wishes, so it is always the perfect time to create eggs with symbols wishing for good health, long life, strength and protection and other good things. 



$75 per person (cash/check) or $78 (credit card) includes use of all supplies. Please contact me for more information or to sign up! $10 discount for WNC residents – mention code: WNC2026.

title: Artist Talk with Karen Sixkiller: Cherokee Water Beetle Brings Sacred Earth to North Carolina
description:
Artist Talk with Karen Sixkiller: Cherokee Water Beetle Brings Sacred Earth to North Carolina
with Karen Sixkiller 
Tuesday, April 28  |  5:30 – 7 pm 
REGISTER HERE 
Any remaining tickets will be sold at the door on Tuesday. 
Learn about how one of the oldest Cherokee stories inspired Artist Karen Sixkiller to create the new ‘Sacred Earth’ sculptural installation at The North Carolina Arboretum.  Sixkiller explores the aspects of magical realism and symbolism that combine her larger-than-life water beetle with the faceted geometric “mud” he perches on. Follow the technical journey of Karen Sixkiller’s simple clay maquette through the process of becoming a large bronze piece of public art. 
Karen Sixkiller is a contemporary sculptor residing on the Olympic Peninsula of Washington state. Sixkiller creates sculptures using metal, ceramic, glass beads, leather/suede and fabric. As a Cherokee Nation citizen much of her work is informed by Native American understandings or stories. Cherokee Nation has purchased many of Karen Sixkiller’s ceramic and mixed media sculptural pieces for display in official buildings. She has permanent public art installations in Tahlequah OK, Olympia and Port Angeles WA, and now Asheville NC; as well as several temporary installations in Coeur d’Alene ID, Olympia WA and Lake Oswego OR. Her work has been featured at multiple Indigenous and non-Indigenous art shows.

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

location: Little Jumbo, 241 Broadway St, Asheville, NC, 28801
description:
The Empyrean Trio ascends to the highest sphere of musical expression, where Sanders, Page, and Hall commune in the celestial realm of pure improvisation. Like ancient philosophers who believed the empyrean was the highest heaven—a place of fire and light beyond the physical world—this trio inhabits the ethereal space where earthbound genres dissolve into transcendent musical dialogue. 
Their original compositions float between the terrestrial and the sublime, oscillating from groove-laden explorations that anchor listeners to the physical realm, to free-form adventures that lift consciousness into the empyrean heights of pure sonic possibility. Through jazz, rock, blues, and world music influences refined by years of improvisational alchemy, the trio channels the luminous fire of creative spontaneity. 
In this rarefied atmosphere, Sanders’ guitar becomes a conduit between the material and immaterial, Page’s bass provides the gravitational pull that keeps the music tethered to human experience, while Hall’s percussion creates the rhythmic cosmos in which their empyrean visions unfold. 
The Empyrean Trio: 

Zack Page – Acoustic & Electric Bass
Alan Hall – Drums
Jay Sanders – Guitar and Effects


Together: architecture in four dimensions. Three virtuosos deciding atmospheric constraints are suggestions that can be ignored with sufficient escape velocity.

title: Sculpt Your Own Water Beetle
description:
Sculpt Your Own Water Beetle
with Karen Sixkiller 
Wednesday, April 29  |  12 – 4pm 
REGISTER HERE 
Many of our oldest Cherokee stories feature small, humble creatures who accomplish the most important things!  Learn a little more about the Grandmother Spider bringing fire and Water Beetle creating earth stories while we celebrate spiders and insects by learning how to sculpt your own Water Beetle. 
All necessary supplies will be provided except a rock (about the size of two fists or bigger) so be sure to bring your own for the class! Students will go home with an air-dry clay Water Beetle mounted to their rock. 
Karen Sixkiller is a contemporary sculptor residing on the Olympic Peninsula of Washington state. Sixkiller creates sculptures using metal, ceramic, glass beads, leather/suede and fabric. As a Cherokee Nation citizen much of her work is informed by Native American understandings or stories. Cherokee Nation has purchased many of Karen Sixkiller’s ceramic and mixed media sculptural pieces for display in official buildings. She has permanent public art installations in Tahlequah OK, Olympia and Port Angeles WA, and now Asheville NC; as well as several temporary installations in Coeur d’Alene ID, Olympia WA and Lake Oswego OR. Her work has been featured at multiple Indigenous and non-Indigenous art shows.

description:

with Dan Lazar 
Wednesday, April 29  |  1:30 – 3pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Elective 
REGISTER HERE 
Join Dan Lazar on this walk and talk designed to point out signs of life awakening in springtime. Wildflowers are blooming, amphibians are mating, and birds are returning to their nesting habitats. Opportunities for learning in place are far from dormant in this or any season at the Arboretum! 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Dan Lazar served for many years as the director of education at the Western North Carolina Nature Center, followed by several years as executive director of the Colburn Earth Science Museum. Dan has a degree in forest biology from the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry and has been an instructor in the Blue Ridge Naturalist program since 2005.

Self-Care and Community of Practice Led by Black Facilitators, for the Black Community.

About this Event
"Caring for myself is not self - indulgence; it is self-preservation, and that is an act of political warfare." Audre Lorde

This is an invitation specifically for persons who identify as Black or African American and are overwhelmed with the injustice of the world and are ready to create space in their lives for self-care as we fight for justice for all! (We offer a parallel session for Allies to connect, learn and find support in their work to dismantle racism at allies.eventbrite.com)

We believe Black people deserve a space to relax, reassess, and realign ourselves.

We are a collective of Black stress-management & wellness instructors inspired by human values.

We are here to facilitate your journey of trauma-relief and stress-management.

Imagine how much more energy you will have and how much more powerful you will be when you cut your stress levels in half!

And it can be done in just a few minutes using nothing but your own breath...

Over the last 10 years, we've taught over 100,000 people to do just that.
The key is that your breath is directly linked to your emotions.

This 1-Hour Restorative Session Includes:
-Open, safe space for sharing and self-care for Black people
-Facilitated discussion
-Breath work and meditation

Led by Black facilitators, certified in stress and trauma relief.
Unleash the Hidden Healing Power of the Breath

title: Southern Appalachian Birds Through the Seasons
description:
Southern Appalachian Birds Through the Seasons
with Carlton Burke 
Thursday, April 30  |  12 – 4pm 
BRN – Core 
REGISTER HERE 
Since birds are capable of long distance flights and many engage in annual migration rituals, their presence in our area often changes in relation to the seasons of the year.  In this class we will discuss the seasonal patterns of southern Appalachian birds and focus on some of the major species and their annual life cycles. As part of this program, there will be a “lab” portion where students will be able to meet some live birds and participate in other hands-on components to deepen the learning. 
Carlton Burke is a naturalist and educator who operates Carolina Mountain Naturalists, an educational service which offers wildlife and nature educational programs throughout western North Carolina. He also was on the staff of the western North Carolina Nature Center in Asheville for over 25 years as the Curator of Exhibits. Carlton co-hosts a weekly radio program NATURE NEWS and is also a NC state and federally licensed wildlife rehabilitator.

title: Volunteer opportunity @ Manna Food Bank
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
## **AVL Digital Nomads Volunteer Day at MANNA FoodBank**

## **Hunger hides in plain sight in Asheville and surrounding communities.**

Many of our neighbors are struggling in silence — facing empty shelves and impossible choices.
Let’s show up and do something about it.
Join **AVL Digital Nomads** for a volunteer shift at **MANNA FoodBank**, where we’ll work together to:

* Sort donations
* Bag bulk food items
* Date-check perishable goods
* Support the team keeping our community fed

Together, we can help create a more caring Asheville where no one goes without a meal.

***

## **What to Expect**

If it’s your first time volunteering at MANNA, here’s a quick walkthrough:

* Plan to arrive a few minutes early at the former FedEx warehouse
* Turn left into the **volunteer parking lot**
* Walk past the turnstile fence and enter the warehouse
* Continue down the hallway past the bathrooms and fridges
* You’ll find a small lounge area with high-top tables where volunteers gather

MANNA staff will usually greet you somewhere between the parking lot and the lounge.
There will be individual volunteers in addition to our group, so:

* Look for other **AVL Digital Nomads**
* Introduce yourself and connect with new arrivals
* We’ll coordinate with simple name tags

Once everyone is checked in:

* MANNA staff will give a **brief safety overview**
* Then assign tasks for the day

They are very accommodating, and there are usually multiple types of tasks available if you have any limitations.

***

## **Important Details (Please Read)**

### Location

MANNA FoodBank
99 Broadpointe Drive, Mills River, NC
*Doors open 10 minutes before the shift — **please arrive a 15 minutes early**.*

### Liability Waiver

* Waivers will be provided **on-site**
* All volunteers must sign upon arrival
* Volunteers 17 and under require a parent or guardian signature

### Dress Code

* **Closed-toe shoes are required** (no exceptions)
* Wear comfortable clothes you don’t mind getting a little dirty

### What to Bring

* Water or your preferred beverage
* Light snacks will be available

### Guidelines

To maintain a safe and welcoming environment:

* **Nicotine-Free Facility**
* No smoking, vaping, or nicotine use inside or within fenced areas
* Items must be stored in your vehicle
* Designated smoking area is at the far end of the parking lot
* **Substance-Free Workplace**
* No alcohol, drugs, or impairing substances (including THC/Kratom)
* **Age Requirement**
* Volunteers must be **10 years or older**

This is a great opportunity to connect with the AVL Digital Nomads community while giving back in a meaningful way.
Come be part of it

title: Camino de Asheville. Section 4 - Approx 6.4 miles.
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
Join me for an evening hike through the hills east of downtown Asheville, exploring Windswept Dr., Helen's Bridge, and downtown.

**Meeting Spot:**
We'll gather at the Depot St. parking lot. GPS: 35.57991, -82.56468

**Pace:**
We'll be walking at a brisk 2.5 to 3.0 mph, leaning more toward 3.0 mph, even uphill. Please be mindful of your fitness level, but don’t worry—we'll take breaks at a few spots to let everyone catch up. While we’ll pause, we can’t wait too long, so come ready for a solid workout!

**No-Shows:**
I’ll be keeping an eye on no-shows. If you RSVP and don’t show up without changing your RSVP or letting me know ahead of time, or you may end up on the waitlist for future hikes.

**Waitlist:**
Regular hikers may get bumped up from the waitlist because I want to emphasize community first, but if you are a regular that stops attending for a few months, you could lose that priority. Make sure to check your RSVP status, even on the day of the hike, as it might change at the last minute! If you're still on the waitlist, please don't show up. Plus-ones for people on the waitlist aren’t allowed—let's keep it fair for those eager to join!

**Bringing a Plus-One:**
If you’re bringing a friend, please select the +1 option when you RSVP or edit your response. It helps me keep an accurate headcount! Make sure your guest is also up for the pace and distance.

**Optional Rucking:**
I will bring along a weighted pack (rucking) for an extra challenge, but it's totally optional! Rucking is great training for backpacking. If you’re carrying more than 15 lbs, I recommend a proper backpack designed for heavy loads to prevent discomfort or injury. If you’re new to this, start light!

title: Four-Hand Piano Trio
location: NC
description:
AmiciMusic continues their Music at the Museum series with a program entitled Four-Hand Piano Trio on Thursday, April 30 at 6:30pm. 
The concert features an international ensemble of musicians—Vadim Tchikil, violin (from France/Russia), Jacques-Pierre Malan, cello (from South Africa), Francesco Cipolletta, piano (from Italy), and pianist/artistic director Daniel Weiser. 
They will perform a program featuring exciting music for violin, cello, and four-hand piano, a very rare and unique combination.  They will play two of the four quartets by Romantic composer Hermann Berens for this combination, as well as some spirited arrangements of the Brahms Hungarian Dances and Liszt’s Rhapsody no. 2. 
AmiciMusic is an award-winning non-profit chamber music organization dedicated to performing intimate, high-quality concerts in non-traditional spaces and to breaking down barriers between performers and audiences through fun, informative talks before each piece is played.  It should be a spectacular show you will not want to miss! 
Purchase Tickets 
  
The Steinway piano is available to the Asheville Art Museum through the courtesy of the Asheville Chamber Music Series.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Craven Gap Out-and-Back -- 5 mi, 800 ft. elev. gain
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**[Sign ups open Sunday, April 26th, 8:00 PM]**

This segment of the Mountain-to-Sea Trail was devastated by Hurricane Helene and closed for well over a year. But now it's back! If you're familiar with this hike, the first mile was radically altered. After that, it looks a little more "normal."

From the Craven Gap parking lot, we cross the Parkway and head south on the Mountain-to-Sea Trail. It's hilly but doesn't add up to much elevation gain. We'll take a short break 2.5 miles out, then return the way we came. It's more scenic than in the past due to lots of new vistas that used to be blocked by trees. Otherwise, just your basic, beautiful, winding forest trail. At our pace (about 2.4 mph), I'd give it a 3.5/10 difficulty rating. We should be back in the parking lot soon after noon.

Well-behaved dogs are welcome, but Forestry Service regulations require leashes.

**\*\*\* CARPOOLING STRONGLY RECOMMENDED \*\*\***
The Craven Gap parking lot used to be large, but now it's small due to reconstruction. Please try to work out carpooling with others on the hike. Depending on where you're coming from, good places to rendezvous may be (1) Ingles on Tunnel Rd. (closest to the downtown tunnel), which is near Town Mountain Rd., (2) Harris-Teeter on Merrimon Ave next to Trader Joe's, (3) Folk Art Center. I'll be happy to bring several people from my downtown location.

**MEETING TIME AND PLACE**

Click here for the [location on Google Maps](https://bit.ly/416noPy). Better yet, search for the **intersection of the Blue Ridge Parkway and Town Mountain Road**. From the intersection of College St. & Town Mtn. Rd. in downtown Asheville, the Craven Gap parking lot is 6.3 miles northeast on Town Mtn. Rd.

We'll meet at **9:00 AM,** so shoot for an 8:50 arrival. After formalities and intros, we'll set out by 9:05.

**GUESTS**

If you'd like to bring a guest, please have them join the Asheville Hiking Group and sign up for the hike independently.

**COURTESY TO WAITLISTERS (Please!!)**

Only sign up if you \*truly\* plan to come. If you must cancel, please change your status to "Not Going" as soon as possible. Avoid dropping out within 18 hours of the hike so wait-listers can have sufficient notice. And please please PLEASE don't be a no-show.

We'll watch the weather and post a cancellation message by 7:00 AM on the morning of the hike if the forecast is >50% chance of precipitation.

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

title: Scenic AVL Wildcard - Hendersonville - With AVL Camino Society
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**Overview:** This hike is offered as a monthly training hike with the WNC Asheville Chapter of the American Society of Pilgrims on the Camino. The route has been announced on the WNC Camino Group [Facebook Group Page](https://www.facebook.com/groups/AVLCamino/announcements).

This route starts with a five mile loop, a coffee break, and a figure eight. We will stop at Southern Streams coffee to chat about Camino preparation and the experience of walking the different routes, including the Frances, the Norte, and the Portuguese. If you are unfamiliar with the Camino, here are a few links to learn more:

*[American Pilgrims on the Camino](https://americanpilgrims.org/iwpmap_directory/western-north-carolina/)
- [Stingy Nomads Camino](https://stingynomads.com/camino-de-santiago-walking-guide/)
*[Gronze Camino Planner](https://www.gronze.com/)

**Distance:** This hike is made up of three sections, all crossing the Ecusta trail. You can join and hike as much or as little as you want 5 miles, 7.5 or 10.5) For those who are just starting their training, come out and do the first or second half!

***9:30am **- Meet at First Congregational Church, 1735 5th Ave W, Hendersonville, NC 2873
*** First section is a five mile loop. **There is a short but steep climb up to Davis Mountain Road, with a short stretch along a gravel road. Pace will be 3.0 mph. The loop ends at Southern Streams coffee house, which is across from the church where we start.

*** 11:00 am **- Southern Streams Coffee house, near FCC church. 30 minute coffee break and camino chat. (if you want to sleep in, meet us here at 11 ish)

***Second Section: **Starting at about 11:30 am from Southern Streams coffee, continue through lower Laurel Park. For those who want to exit, you can return to the church on the Ecusta Trail for a total of about 7 miles.

*** Last Section: **To downtown and St. James Church, returning via Ecusta Trail. 10.5 miles total distance. We plan to arrive at the church around 1:15 pm.

**Elevation Gain: **800 ft total if you do the full 10.5.
**Pace: **3.0-3.2 mph
**Surface: **Road, with short stretch on gravel road.
**Rating: **Strenuous for distance, if you do the whole thing.
**Features:**
*Neighborhood charm, last of the spring color, Hendersonville downtown, St James church.
*No bears. There may be geese or ducks on Rhododendron lake.

**Cautions: **There are a few stretches on busy roads where we will need to walk single file.

**Full Route: **[Laurel Park Loop](https://www.alltrails.com/explore/map/laurel-park-loop-improved-3937230?u=i&sh=ifwm3x)

**Parking: **We are meeting at the First Congregational Church. Please carpool if possible.

**Gear: **2L water, snacks, cash for coffee at Southern Streams.
**Dogs: **On leash the entire time.
**After Event: **Some of us will go to [ El Sol y La Luna, ](https://maps.app.goo.gl/pfvgkMsJztNXAANi9)Cali-Mex, after the hike.

**Scenic Asheville Series: **This hike counts as a Wildcard substitute on my Scenic Asheville Series. There are 9 [hikes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11ewlUM9OV8I4npc1cNNsSYOnXI0QPw2isAleXdFzEbI/edit?usp=drivesdk) in the series; hike them all and receive an [attractive badge](https://docs.google.com/drawings/d/1goXUXfzUBqhB4_UeCxodlk4ZPeCCgqZrWK2EUJvk_vI/edit) for your backpack. Check your status [HERE](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1XUm-X1_OhxKIi8JU5rhjsW37cAl4yYx8yB_NEjjI5Lk/edit?gid=0#gid=0).

**On-Time Departure**
We will start by walking the labyrinth at the First Congregational Church, so this is a pretty relaxed start.

- Please change your RSVP as soon as you know you can't make it.
*If you have questions, call the hike leader (Gracen) at 828-290-0886.

**Guests:** For this hike, there are no guest restrictions. Bring them with you.

**Disclaimer and Release of Liability:**
This activity involves hiking on city streets that may have traffic and/or hiking on natural surfaces. Participants are responsible for their safety on streets and trails. The organizer of this trip is a volunteer and not a professional guide. The function of the organizer is only to organize this trip. If you sign up or participate in this event you acknowledge that you freely and voluntarily agree to assume all risks of injuries, illnesses, and damages arising from, as a result of, and associated with this event. You are responsible for any guests, dogs or other companions you bring with you. title: Updated: The Biltmore Farm Trail Is Fairly Flat and a 6 Mile Round Trip—Join Us!
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
**Update: The Farm Trail and the Arbor Trace Trail are currently closed (as of March 8). If still closed on May 2, we will walk the Lagoon Trail instead. The start point is the same, but the distance is shorter.**

In front of the Antler Hill Barn, by the Playground, there is a picnic shelter known as the Antler Hill Pavillion. We will meet there at 9:30 a.m.

We will walk the seldom-done Farm Trail along the French Broad River edge of the estate property, mostly out and back. Biltmore says it is a 6-mile (10 KM) round trip.

Dress for the weather. Bring a protein snack and water. Walking sticks only if you want them since the walk will be mostly level. Tennis shoes should be okay, unless it has rained a lot recently, in which case light hiking boots would be better. Dogs are welcome. Trail strollers should work ok.

You will need a grounds pass, so arrive no later than 9 a.m. to purchase it and let me know so we will wait to start the walk until you have joined us. We actually recommend the purchase of an annual pass, as we will be walking on the estate grounds several times in the coming year.

title: Healing Threads ATELIER with guest artist Elizabeth Garlington
location: ArtPlay Studio, 53 Orange Street, Asheville, NC, 28801
description:
The ATELIER at ArtPlay is a new type of offering designed to support your creative process within a circle of community while receiving guidance and inspiration from an artist. It is neither a traditional class nor an open studio. Instead, it is a gently guided creative experience. 
This session is open to those who have previously taken Elizabeth’s Healing Threads workshop, as well as those who are seeking dedicated exploration time and guidance for their fiber or stitch-based creative projects. 
During this three-hour creative immersion, you’ll enter an extended period of intentional play and experimentation with fiber materials. With Elizabeth as your guide, you will deepen and expand your creative process while continuing to explore the layering of fabrics with stitching. Along the way, you may also discover the meditative and calming qualities that often emerge through this type of handwork. 
In this studio-based Healing Threads Atelier, participants will receive supportive, responsive guidance as they continue developing fiber-based works already in progress, while also being encouraged in the initiation of new pieces. As art is made in community, each participant contributes an important energy to the Healing Threads Atelier circle. 
Participants are invited to bring personal works-in-progress, completed pieces they wish to share with the group, and any materials that support their individual projects. Elizabeth will also have a selection of fiber-based supplies available in the studio.

title: Maxwell, Pressley Cove(s) loop
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
N.B. will be watching the weather forecast, and if need be will just roll the hike into Sunday for those who have that flexibility (if it happens)

this is about a 5 mile (maybe a bit less) loop with 1000-ish feet of elevation gain in the ranger station section of Pisgah.

the starting point is the newer gravel parking lot near Avery creek about 1.6 miles in on the forest service road leading to the stables, Twin Falls etc. just past the Bennett Gap trail. carpooling is encouraged

from the starting point, ascent to Maxwell Cove is via an unmarked trail further down the road, with an approx 1 mile climb. We then wend our way up Maxwell, past an interesting historical ruin to Pressley Gap, where the Black Mountain trail crosses. Then back down Maxwell to Pressley Cove trail, which leads back down to the parking area.

well behaved dogs are welcome on this hike

say 2 - 2.5 mph pace

gear up as appropriate, trekking poles are an option. bring a snack as we'll take a break mid-hike. and plenty of water

ground rules:

if you sign up, show up or change your status. a no-show may undercut a motivated wait-lister. (repeated no-shows will have consequences) likewise, if you're on the wait list at the time of the hike, don't presume to just show up

2 ) be sure you are in adequate physical shape to complete the event

3) show consideration. emphasize group effort and group cohesion. I hike for stress reduction and want to keep it that way.

description:

location: Trackside Studios, 375 Depot Street, Asheville, 28801
description:
This is the ideal class for someone who has never painted or struggles with plein air!!! Come join in the fun! Great for beginners & intermediates! 
3pm – 5pm – in classroom @ Trackside Studio where we will get prepared. This will allow us to gatherer our materials, prep our palettes by premixing paint, and go over the fundamentals of plein air. 
* Then we will take our individual vehicles to Carrier Park right around the corner* 
Between 5pm & 6pm we will snack & set up – By 6pm we will be ready to capture the “Golden Hour” on canvas. We will wrap things up by 7:30pm and get on road just before dark. 
Workshop Description: 
A workshop focused on painting el plein air (outdoors on location) to capture natural light, atmosphere, and landscape subjects, teaching fundamental techniques like color mixing, composition, value, and simplifying scenes, suitable for all levels emphasizing learning from direct observation and the environment. 
A plein air workshop (from the French en plein air, meaning “in the open air”) is an educational art session focused on painting or drawing directly from nature outdoors. Unlike studio painting, which often uses photographs as reference, plein air artists must capture shifting light, atmosphere, and moving subjects in real-time. 
Registration and info on what to bring are at https://www.tracksidestudios.com/classes

title: May 2nd An Evening of Spicy/Sensual Snuggles
description:
Asheville Cuddle Collective
Please note- If you want to attend this event you need to purchase a ticket- We advertise in many places and only paid tickets will reserve your space.[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-2nd-an-evening-of-sensual-snuggles)**[CLICK HERE TO PURCHASE YOU TICKET AND RESERVE YOUR SPACE FOR THIS EVENT.](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-2nd-an-evening-of-sensual-snuggles)**[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/may-2nd-an-evening-of-sensual-snuggles)

**What is a Sensual Snuggle Event?**
This is a sweet & welcoming event where we practice and use verbal consent to connect and share touch. We talk about boundaries and practice both saying and receiving a “no”. In this space it is common to see people cuddle, share massage, have their hair brushed, kiss, expose nipples, play, laugh, cry, and be vulnerable. This is a sober space where we can relax and connect with other humans who are seeking touch based connection.
We strive for this to be a safe event. Safe touch enhances our ability to connect with and trust people. When we are in a space of safety, we are able to relax, feel comfort, and be vulnerable.

**Our Agreements:**
1- We ask for what we want an wait for a yes before touching others.
2- We say no if we don’t want to do something.
3- We try to receive a no with grace and not take it personally.
4- We arrive on time, clean (as scent free as possible), and sober.
5- We keep our pants/shorts on at this event. (Tops are optional; this is a sensual space, not a sexual space.)
6- We are here to connect with others. Connection can be verbal, platonic, or spicy!
7- We welcome diversity. Isms and Phobias are not welcome here!

**Who should attend:**
People who are interested in safely exploring touch and sensuality with strangers. This includes people who are single, people who are not single, couples, folks who are new to town and looking for connection, people of all/any genders and sexual orientations, people of all ages (18 and up). People who understand and respect consent, who will take care of themselves and people around them. This event is queer-normative. The guest list will include all genders, orientations, ages, and personalities. If that’s not your thing… This is not the event for you.
***Who should NOT attend:***
-People who are only looking for a sex party.
-People who do not understand and respect consent.
-People who have extreme fear of setting and speaking their personal boundaries; in order to create a safe space we need to know that you will say “no” if you feel a no.
-People who are homophobic, racist, sexist, ageist, ableist…
-People under 18 years of age.
***Schedule of the Evening***

* 6:50pm Doors Open, Mix & Mingle
* 7:00pm We gather in a circle to meet each other, build a container, cover consent and boundary setting and discuss event agreements. Then we will play a few intimacy building games to meet and connect with other people in the room. Please make sure you arrive on-time!
* 8:15pm Once the container is built we will have self directed snuggling and sensual interactions until the end of the party.
* 10:50pm Closing Circle; a time to re-center and connect as a group to verbally share anything that came up at the event or to voice gratitude to someone(s) you enjoyed interacting with.
* 11:00pm cleanup & head home; you are welcome to help.

**We take individual and group safety seriously!** If you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at this event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

These events are not "gender balanced"[. Check out our website for more information about this decision. ](http://holdmeavl.com/why-i-dont-gender-balance-events/)

**Simple definitions/clarifications-** Platonic- marked by the absence of romance or sex.
Most of the interactions we have with friends and strangers are platonic.
Sensual- gratification of the senses or the indulgence of appetite.
We might feel sensual when we feel someone's breath on our neck or experience a extra long and slow caress.
Sexual- having or involving sex.
Often involving one more more peoples genitals; perhaps seeking orgasm.
\*Refund Policy- Full refund if you cancel 7 days before the event or you cancel due to illness, emergency, or direct exposure to covid. Credit towards a future event if you cancel more than 3 days before an event. No refund if you cancel within 2 days of the event or no-show.

Each student will be provided with several sets of printing cards and fabric patches and tea towels to choose from. 
All materials you need for this class are provided but please feel free to bring one (1) item of clothing to make more magic onto from your home collection. Solid, light colors work best- and nothing too textured.

title: Spring Botanicals in Watercolors with local artist Casi Fordham
location: ArtPlay Studio, 53 Orange Street, Asheville, NC, 28801
description:
Celebrate the arrival of Spring with creativity, community & fresh flowers at your table! 
In this class you will learn the foundational techniques in watercolor painting, using fresh Spring blooms as your inspiration. We will have plenty of blooms available for you, and if you have some blooms from your garden or elsewhere that you love, feel free to bring some along! 
Local watercolor artist Casi Fordham will guide you in learning various wet into wet watercolor techniques, dry-brushing & using dark & light values as you build layers of color and shape to create your blooms, adding details and embellishments afterward. 
Allowing the pigment and water to interact as they expand across the page together is a great way to trust the creative process as it unfolds. Watercolors have a way of leading and surprising you if you allow them to! 
You will begin with a step-by-step watercolor demo where you will warm-up with Casi’s guidance, and then transition into several rounds of layering and painting on your background papers. We’ll explore basic techniques, break down the elements of building values, guided by demos each step along the way. You will bring home your practice pieces as well as a larger piece you’ll work up to. 
PLEASE BRING WITH YOU: a vase for your flower (s) that you will place in front of you for visual reference. 
A light afternoon snack and a glass of wine will be served. 
All materials provided. No experience needed. 
Come play, learn & create!

BOYB - Bring Your Own Book and rant or rave about your current Fantasy or Sci-fi titles! We will either be in the large room inside or out back on the patio depending on weather.

**What is a Silent Book Club?**
Referred to as "Introvert's Happy Hour", Silent Book clubs allow readers to engage with each other without the commitment of reading a shared title. Community members gather in the same place, have some casual chit chat, and then read silently together. **This group will focus on Fantasy and Sci-Fi titles (subgenres & related genres are welcome!)**

**How does it work?**
For the first 15-30 mins we will gather and engage in introductions. Feel free to discuss your recent favorites, mention a title that lives in your head rent free, or ask for recommendations! The best part of the Silent Book Club is being able to talk shop with other readers!

Once settled in we will dedicate 45 minutes to silent reading. Your book can be traditional, ebook, or audiobook. Read at your own pace!

Afterwards we will go around show-and-tell style and share what we read with the group. Feel free to share as much or as little as you want! Organic dialogue welcome!

title: Craven Gap
description:
Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club 2.0
This is a fairly undulating hike. It's narrow at first with some rocky steps and then narrow and rooty for most of the way until halfway when there's a short climb to the 2.5 mile mark. We go about 2.7 to 2.9 mph.

Well behaved dogs on leashes are welcome to attend.

When you arrive, park at the gravel lot on the other side of the road, closest to Town Mountain. You'll see some people gathering by their cars.

Mountains-to-Sea-Trail hikes are designed for fitness and community among people who are already reasonably fit. It's not an endurance hike by any means, but it is designed so we can get our hearts beating a bit while still being able to have a conversation and meet new people.
When you arrive, we'll circle up and introduce ourselves briefly. There will be a person who is a sweep. This person is the person who walks last and makes sure no one gets lost.

We leave the parking spot at 9:10. If someone needs a nature break, we wait fo you, but it's not a hike where we stop and take photos or frequent breaks. We basically keep hiking until the 1/2 way mark, then turn around after a short (approximately 5 minute) break. Then we keep that same pace on the way back. If we get on a trail right at 9:10, we are normally finished around 10:50.

These are out and back hikes, meaning that we hike in and turn around half way to return back.

title: Game Night @ Archetype West Asheville
description:
Asheville 20s-40s Social Group
\*\*This is a collaboration with the Asheville's Bored Game Geeks\*\*

Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!
**Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!**

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers!
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**.

**Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death!
No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.***

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary.

See you at the table!

title: AVL Digital Nomads - Book Club!
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**May Selection - *Beautiful Country: A Memoir of an Undocumented Childhood* by Qian Julie Wang**

In Chinese, the word for America, Mei Guo, translates directly to “beautiful country.” Yet when seven-year-old Qian arrives in New York City in 1994 full of curiosity, she is overwhelmed by crushing fear and scarcity. In China, Qian’s parents were professors; in America, her family is “illegal” and it will require all the determination and small joys they can muster to survive. Inhabiting her childhood perspective with exquisite lyric clarity and unforgettable charm and strength, Qian Julie Wang has penned an essential American story about a family fracturing under the weight of invisibility, and a girl coming of age in the shadows, who never stops seeking the light.

**Welcome** to our robust and engaging Book Club! We're a small, friendly group dedicated to fostering lively discussions about our monthly book selections. Whether you've read the entire book, just a few chapters, or even if you're simply curious about the title, we'd love to have you join us!

**Meeting Schedule**: We gather on the First Tuesday of every month for our book discussions.

What sets us apart is our small group size and directed discussions. This intimate setting allows for deeper, more engaging conversations where everyone's voice can be heard. It's the perfect environment for those who love to dive deep into themes, characters, and the intricacies of storytelling.

So whether you're a seasoned bookworm or just dipping your toes into the world of literature, we invite you to join us. Let's explore new worlds, challenge our perspectives, and forge new friendships - one book at a time!

**June Pick: *Is A River Alive: A Journey with Water* by Robert MacFarlane**

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

WI-FI: Yes!

PARKING: Street parking in metered spots is free after 6pm. Closest municipal garages ($2/hour) are Wall St. & Coxe Street/Sears Alley.

location: Fine Arts Theatre, 36 Biltmore Avenue, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
After the loss of her husband and father, Sabena Weathers (Radha Mitchell) fights to preserve her family’s cosmetics empire while facing a hostile takeover. Seeking refuge, she retreats to a remote mountaintop garden cottage, where a chance encounter with a simple gardener (William Miller) sparks a powerful journey of love, self-discovery, and transformation. Rooted in quiet mystery and emotional truth, THE GARDENER explores loss, healing, and the courage to realize one’s true self. 
LOCAL CONNECTIONS 
Much of the movie was filmed locally in Franklin and Highlands, NC. In addition, a local creative team worked together to produce the book. The book is the vision of Director Dabney Day, and was co-designed by Dabney and local RADA artist/designer Andrea Kulish Wilhelm. The book was illustrated with gorgeous original watercolor paintings by Asheville RADA artist, Olga Dorenko, was printed locally by Rocky Kenworthy at Dot Editions, and the binding was done by Kimberly Obee of Wishing Flower Press and Bindery in Black Mountain. The Gardener will screen at the Fine Arts Theater in Asheville on May 6. Writer/Director/Producer Dabney Day will be in attendance and will have a Q& A at the end. https://www.thegardenermovie.com/

title: AVL UX - A First “get to know” the UX community
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
AVL UX (hosted by AVL Digital Nomads) is Asheville’s new meetup for UX, product, and research folks. This first event is casual and low-pressure and focuses on- quick intros, small-group chats, and a short “what should we do next?” moment.

What if Asheville had a regular place where UX people could actually find each other and it without, feeling like a stiff “networking event”? **AVL UX is Asheville’s new meetup for UX, product, and research meant to build and connect the local community to shape what the**
**UX scene here becomes.**

This first gathering is intentionally **friendly + low-pressure**. Come as you are: working designer, researcher, PM, engineer, student, career-switcher, or just UX-curious. The goal is simple: meet people, trade notes, and leave with new connections (and a clearer idea of what AVL UX should be next).

**What to expect**

* Quick welcomes + name tags (so it’s easy to meet people).
* Casual small-group conversations and prompts (And hopefully no awkward interactions).
* A short “what should AVL UX do next?” moment (talks, portfolio nights, design jams, a Config watch party 2026, etc.)

**A few topics up for discussion**

* **What’s your Asheville UX Scene?:** Where is everyone and what is everyone doing in Asheville? Why UX here as the industry is rather small
* **Design-to-code + vibe-coding workflows:** what’s actually working with tools like Figma Make/MCP + Cursor—and what breaks in real teams?
* **Accessibility is becoming the baseline:** how are you baking WCAG 2.2 into design + dev early (instead of last-minute fixes)?
* **Design systems + tokens in 2026:** how do we keep tokens clean, scalable, and synced between design + code without “token rot”?
* **Calm, mindful UX:** how do we reduce cognitive load and create more “human” experiences instead of noisy, attention-grabby UI?

For our first meeting we’ll go to Hi-Wire Brewing in RAD. Easy to get to with plenty of parking. A great assortment of both alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages. Typically there is a food truck as well.

Looking forward to meeting everyone and launching our new UX community!

That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Craven Gap
description:
Asheville Mountains-to-Sea Trail Hiking Club 2.0
This is a fairly undulating hike. It's narrow at first with some rocky steps and then narrow and rooty for most of the way until halfway when there's a short climb to the 2.5 mile mark. We go about 2.7 to 2.9 mph.

Well behaved dogs on leashes are welcome to attend.

When you arrive, park at the gravel lot on the other side of the road, closest to Town Mountain. You'll see some people gathering by their cars.

Mountains-to-Sea-Trail hikes are designed for fitness and community among people who are already reasonably fit. It's not an endurance hike by any means, but it is designed so we can get our hearts beating a bit while still being able to have a conversation and meet new people.
When you arrive, we'll circle up and introduce ourselves briefly. There will be a person who is a sweep. This person is the person who walks last and makes sure no one gets lost.

We leave the parking spot at 9:10. If someone needs a nature break, we wait fo you, but it's not a hike where we stop and take photos or frequent breaks. We basically keep hiking until the 1/2 way mark, then turn around after a short (approximately 5 minute) break. Then we keep that same pace on the way back. If we get on a trail right at 9:10, we are normally finished around 10:50.

These are out and back hikes, meaning that we hike in and turn around half way to return back.

description:
Asheville 20s-40s Social Group
Join us for Asheville Swing Night on **May 8th** for an evening of swing dancing, great music, and a fun beginner-friendly lesson. 💃🕺

We’re changing up the lesson format a bit this month based on feedback we received, and we think you’re going to love it.

Deb and Franklin will kick things off with the beginner fundamentals so everyone can learn the basic 6-count footwork and get comfortable with swing dancing. 🎶

Then, those who want to learn more can branch off with them to learn a few fun next-step moves, while the rest of us continue practicing in a relaxed group with help from our experienced dance assistants.

No partner needed. During both the lesson and social dance, most people rotate partners, making it a fun and easy way to meet people and get comfortable in the space.

(Most people come alone, by the way.)

**What dance are we learning?**
Intro Lindy Hop and East Coast Swing.

**How many people come?**
We typically have 55–65 people, and some months much more. It’s open to the public, not just this Meetup group.

**What should I wear?**
Wear shoes that are comfortable to dance in. Heels are not recommended. Leather-soled shoes or comfortable sneakers are best. Dressing up is optional - people wear everything from casual to vintage-inspired outfits.

## Logistics

📍 **Location:** Haw Creek Commons
Parking is onsite, or at Haw Creek Elementary if the lot is full. Just walk across the field to the venue.

🕖 **7:00 PM sharp** — Beginner swing dance lesson
(Please arrive on time, as the lesson builds progressively and is harder to join late if you're brand new.)

💵 **$10 admission** includes both the lesson and dance
Pay at the door (cash or Venmo)

👥 Ages 12+

title: Painting Flowers Abstractly, with local artist Alison Press
location: ArtPlay Studio, 53 Orange Street, Asheville, NC, 28801
description:
A perfect spring art class or Mother’s Day weekend outing! 
This beautiful workshop, created by Alison, is designed for creatives of all levels — especially beginners who are ready to explore abstract painting in an approachable, supportive environment. Whether you’re brand new to painting or have years of experience, you’ll be gently guided while also encouraged to trust your own creative instincts. 
Working with acrylic paints, we’ll explore color, form, line, and value through bold brushstrokes, thick and thin lines, and playful, expressive interpretations of flowers on canvas. The focus will be on painting loosely, discovering your own abstract style, and most importantly — enjoying the process. 
During class, Alison will guide you step by step in creating boldly painted flowers using a loose, abstract approach. We’ll begin with a quick charcoal sketch of a floral bouquet still-life directly on the canvas. This initial sketch is not meant to be detailed or precise — it simply serves as a relaxed starting point to help you begin confidently. 
By the end of the workshop, you’ll leave with a vibrant, one-of-a-kind floral painting — and the confidence that comes from painting freely, expressively, and in community.

New Belgium has been a human-powered company from the beginning. title: Exhibition on Screen | Raphael Revealed
location: NC
description:
Marking the 500th anniversary of Raphael’s death, the greatest exhibition ever held of his works took place in Rome. Exhibition on Screen was granted exclusive access to this once-in-a-lifetime show. With over two hundred masterpieces, including paintings and drawings – over a hundred of which have been brought together for the first time – this major exhibition celebrates the life and work of Raffaello Sanzio da Urbino. 
With unprecedented loans from the Louvre, Uffizi, National Gallery of Art, the Prado Museum and more, the exhibition and this film provide an unprecedented opportunity to see the breadth of Raphael’s skill, creativity and ingenuity. Award-winning director Phil Grabsky provides a fresh look at this giant of the Renaissance, and shows why he is considered one of the all-time greats. The film covers his life in Rome, and includes unique footage of the ancient Rome that was such a powerful influence, including rare footage of Nero’s Golden House that Raphael himself visited. 
More than just a painter, Raphael was one of the most extraordinary artists of the Renaissance but is often misunderstood or mythologised. On the basis of this extraordinary exhibition in Rome, this film allows Raphael, for the first time, to be truly revealed. Directed by Phil Grabsky. 
Purchase Tickets

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**From Chatbot to Co-Worker: A Business Guide to AI That Actually Works**
**Speaker:** [Julio Barros](https://www.linkedin.com/in/juliobarros/)

**Description:** Most business owners use AI the way people used the internet in 1996, they check the weather. They type questions into ChatGPT, read the answer, and close the tab. Meanwhile, a quiet revolution is underway: small teams are using AI agents to run real business operations, following up with leads, generating reports, managing content pipelines, and handling customer support autonomously.
The gap between "asking AI questions" and "giving AI a job" is the biggest competitive window most of us will see in our careers. But closing that gap wrong is worse than not closing it at all.
This session walks you through the progression from chatbot to co-worker with live demonstrations, then gives you a practical framework for identifying where to start in your own business - and what order to do it in so you don't automate the wrong thing first.

**General Event Info**
AI Hacks and Hops is a monthly event tailored for non-technical professionals, entrepreneurs, marketers, engineers, or anyone who wants to explore and discuss how to use AI.

Each gathering will feature presentations, stimulating group discussions, and a relaxed atmosphere for enjoying your favorite brews while delving into the world of AI. Topics will range from AI integration in business processes, marketing, content creation, software, ethical considerations, human-AI collaboration strategies, to the latest advancements in AI technology. The informal setting encourages open dialogue, idea exchange, and fosters a collaborative spirit.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Soul Stitches: Autobiographical Embroidery with guest artist Elizabeth Garlington
location: ArtPlay Studio, 53 Orange Street, Asheville, NC, 28801
description:
This two-day immersive workshop explores the intuitive process of embroidered fabric collage. 
We will explore fiber art that explores themes of resilience and healing via the art of hand sewing and embroidered words on fabric as an added element to the collage process. 
Open to all skill levels, students will first learn foundational embroidery techniques by creating a “sampler” of running and back stitches, including lettering. Students will learn to embroider text based on their own journal writings and important quotes. 
Favorite fabrics and/or vintage linen as base fabrics are encouraged as this element will bring an additional layer of meaning to our process/product. This introspective workshop invites personal exploration and collective connection. Inspired by story, life experiences, and playing with many colors of embroidery floss, threads, yarns, and fabrics, students will take inspiration from their daily life and written expression to create an original embroidered work of fabric collage art which could lead to a meditative daily art practice. 
This class is a place to find your own unique making. 
Students are encouraged to bring: any journal writings, meaningful quotes, written expressions, as well as favorite fabrics and/or vintage linen as their base fabric–all bringing an additional layer of meaning to this art form. The purchase of a 6” and 10” embroidery hoop is suggested so that the embroidery process you begin in this workshop can be continued in your own time and space. 
This is a beginner-friendly workshop and no experience is needed! Come as you are!

title: Psychedelic Integration Circle
description:
Psychedelic Society of Asheville
We invite you to gather with us in a safe, confidential, and supportive space to share, reflect, and connect with community.

Integration is a practice of intentionally slowing down, listening inward, and making meaning of our experiences so they can truly support and enrich our lives. Through integration, we can cultivate greater awareness of our thoughts, emotions, and patterns, allowing us to move through life’s changes with greater resilience, clarity, and compassion.

We are delighted to welcome Becca Marshall as our Psychedelic Integration Circle facilitator. Becca is an Integrative Psychotherapist, Aligned Living Coach, Psychedelic Integration Guide, and the founder of ActivXchange. Her work supports individuals navigating major life transitions, whether entering adulthood, stepping into leadership, or guiding others through healing and transformation, with grounded presence and deep care.

This ongoing circle is open to all whether you are simply curious, actively preparing for or integrating psychedelic experiences, or have been walking this path for some time. Our intention is to foster connection, shared wisdom, and mutual support within our ever-growing psychedelic community here in Asheville. All are welcome.

Please note that this is a sober gathering. To ensure the integrity and safety of our space, we do not permit the sale, purchase, or sourcing of any illegal substances or activities at our events. Anyone not honoring these guidelines will be respectfully asked to leave.

This gathering is offered with a suggested $10 donation. No one will be turned away for lack of funds. Contributions help cover venue costs and support future offerings from the Psychedelic Society of Asheville.
